result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the recording first and break the motion into its three beats with slowed playback and a spec table. A is stronger on the fallback for people who won't play video: its keyframe filmstrip is meant to be read as a still, and it tells reviewers what to watch in its first line. A also refuses to invent results. B's labelled timecode overlay is excellent, but it guesses overlap timings it wasn't given, and it offers stills only as a stand-in for clips, not as a fallback for non-viewers. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers lead with the recording, split the motion into its three beats, use the 250ms and 400ms timings and suggest slowed playback. B does better on the fallback: it adds a keyframe filmstrip that reviewers can read without pressing play, and it tells them up front what to watch and in what order. B also says outright not to invent results, while A suggests a rationale sentence and adds a few general format tips that are less tied to presenting the motion.
